name: Bellhop hosting, configuration, startup, health and shutdown
description: What a node does from registration to shutdown: option handling, store selection, schema migration, the client, worker and dashboard registrations, the startup summary, the health check and graceful shutdown. Also holds product-level context (scope, principles, non-goals, phasing, design decisions) as info items. Job-level effects of shutdown live in the jobs module.

entities.name: Store
entities.description: The configured job store as seen by a node.

entities.name: Options
entities.description: Bellhop options after binding configuration and code.

entities.name: Health
entities.description: The result reported by the Bellhop health check on a node.

ears.shall: be a durable background-job library for .NET applications covering fire-and-forget, delayed and recurring jobs, continuations, chains and batches, retries, dead-lettering, cancellation and timeouts, multi-node execution over a shared store, a dashboard, observability and testing support

follow the product principles P1 to P9: three lines to a working system; one obvious way to define a job; correct under concurrency by construction; boring storage; secure and explicit by default; nothing is silent; testable without statics; trustworthy versioning and licensing; build in what everyone installs

requirements.notes: Every consequence listed in the principles table is restated by a concrete requirement elsewhere (P1: NFR-1; P2: TECH-14, TECH-15; P3: INV-103, INV-115, INV-203, TECH-51; P4: TECH-31, TECH-36, TECH-9, TECH-105; P5: REQ-301, INV-120, REQ-9; P6: NFR-51; P7: NFR-53, TECH-12, TECH-102; P8: NFR-20, NFR-37, NFR-18; P9: REQ-6). Kept here as context only.

ears.shall: define a job as data (a name plus a JSON document) with behaviour in a separate DI-constructed handler, so that renames, refactors and rolling deploys cannot break stored jobs

requirements.rationale: Answers the grievances in research.md §1.4 and §1.5; it is the pattern .NET developers know from MediatR, Wolverine, Brighter and MassTransit.

sources.quote: the stored record is a name plus a JSON document, so renames, refactors and rolling deploys cannot break it

ears.shall: not be a message bus, pub/sub system or cross-language job executor
not provide sagas, compensation, human-in-the-loop tasks or long-lived workflow state
offer no plugin API for third-party dashboard pages, job states or claim semantics; extension is through DI hooks and the JSON API only

requirements.rationale: ADR-3, decided by the project owner on 2026-11-03: the most-installed Hangfire plugin functionality is built in instead.

ears.shall: not offer exactly-once execution; delivery is at-least-once with idempotency tooling

not ship in v1: first-party MongoDB or MySQL stores, a hosted SaaS control plane, vendor-specific notification SDKs, remote execution agents, arbitrary script execution from the dashboard, Windows-specific features, or Hangfire's expression-based Enqueue(() => ...) API

requirements.notes: A Hangfire migration guide is promised (NFR-30). Whether a legacy adapter package ships is open (TECH-125).

ears.shall: fail the host's start with a message that names the option and the fix

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (refiner-model F-10, recommended option): StartupFailed fails the host's start, the .NET convention for options validation. Process exit also releases a held migration lock (REQ-56, TECH-126).

sources.quote: Options MUST be validated at startup (ValidateOnStart) with messages that name the option and the fix.

ears.shall: treat job delivery as at-least-once: a job may start more than once within the duplicate window, which equals the lease length (LeaseDuration)

requirements.notes: Defined here because several modules rely on it; LeaseDuration itself is REQ-102 in the jobs module.

ears.shall: allow a node mode of Both or ClientOnly, with Both as the default (NodeMode)

requirements.notes: Retired. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: there are no node modes. What a process does is defined only by what it registers: the client, the worker and the dashboard (REQ-52).

ears.shall: start the Bellhop node, validate the options and run the startup checks that need no store (dashboard REQ-301 and REQ-334, recurring REQ-210), then connect to the store, which for Redis includes its EVAL and eviction-policy checks (redis REQ-500, REQ-502, REQ-505), check the schema (failing under REQ-23 or REQ-43) and run the startup checks that read stored data (recurring REQ-236, which reads a store that is not migrated yet), and only then migrate under REQ-22 and, where the worker is registered and the schema version is accepted with no migration pending, reconcile code-defined recurring jobs

requirements.notes: Step order fixed by refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-4 (recommended option): a node that is about to fail validation must not migrate or write to the shared store first, and recurring definitions are reconciled only into a schema the node accepts. refiner-model 2026-11-06 run 2 F-1 (recommended option): every startup check owned by another module has its place in the order, so a node that will fail any startup check never migrates the shared schema or writes recurring definitions. Checks that need no store run with option validation; checks that need the connection or the stored definitions run after the schema check and before any write. Run 3 F-1 (recommended option): the run-2 order stays, because a migration by a node that then fails a check would turn every older node Unhealthy (REQ-32) with no new node running. Recurring REQ-236 therefore runs on an unmigrated store; its own sentence says what it reads there. Run 3 F-2 (recommended option): the Redis EVAL and eviction checks are part of connecting, as redis REQ-500 and TECH-69 already say, so a server without EVAL fails the start with the --lua message instead of the schema message, and never retries for ever as if it were unreachable.

sources.quote: Database connectivity, schema checks and job reconciliation happen in the hosted service, after the host starts.

ears.while: services are being registered and the host has not started
ears.shall: perform no I/O: no store connection, no schema check and no job reconciliation

ears.where: the process runs build-time tooling such as OpenAPI generation or EF Core design-time services
ears.shall: not start the scheduler or any worker
use the in-memory store

ears.if: no store is configured and the environment is not Development
ears.shall: log a warning that the in-memory store is in use, once, before the node is marked running

requirements.notes: Event-driven and once, before running (refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-7, recommended option), so SCN-1's 'exactly one warning' is guaranteed. Same startup event as REQ-53 and REQ-54, with a different consequence.

ears.where: an option is set both in configuration (the Bellhop section) and in code
ears.shall: use the value set in code

sources.quote: All options MUST be bindable from IConfiguration ("Bellhop": { ... }) and overridable in code.

ears.when: the store is reachable, the stored schema version is accepted (REQ-23, REQ-43), no migration is pending under REQ-22, all startup checks have passed, including option validation (REQ-9) and the dashboard checks (dashboard REQ-301, REQ-334), and, where the worker is registered, code-defined recurring jobs have been reconciled (REQ-12)
ears.shall: mark the node running and, where the worker is registered, start the worker and its background duties

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06: 'no migration is pending' (F-2, recommended option) means that with AutoMigrate on the schema must equal the expected version, so REQ-22 always runs first and the migration releases its own lock; the accepted one-older version applies with AutoMigrate off (rolling deploys). The startup checks are named (dashboard findings F-5, recommended option) so the dashboard checks precede 'running' by definition. Run 2 F-2 (recommended option): reconciliation is part of the trigger, so the scheduler always starts on reconciled definitions; recurring REQ-203 and REQ-204 fire while the node is still starting.

ears.when: the store is reachable, the stored schema version is accepted (REQ-23, REQ-43), no migration is pending under REQ-22, all startup checks have passed, including option validation (REQ-9) and the dashboard checks (dashboard REQ-301, REQ-334), and, where the worker is registered, code-defined recurring jobs have been reconciled (REQ-12)
ears.shall: log a one-screen summary with the store and schema version, which of the client, worker, alerts and dashboard are registered, queues and concurrency, the registered job count, recurring jobs with their next run, and the dashboard path and auth mode

requirements.notes: Same event as REQ-18 with a second consequence; the agent should model one action, and the `when` text must stay identical to REQ-18's. The Redis store adds the server family to the summary (REQ-500). Secrets never appear in it (NFR-41).

ears.while: a node has no worker registered
ears.shall: never claim or execute a job on that node

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: node modes are replaced by registrations (REQ-52); a process without AddWorker never runs jobs.

sources.quote: A process without a worker never claims a job or runs a background duty.

ears.shall: default AutoMigrate to true in every environment (AutoMigrate)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (§9 Q4): true everywhere, as STO-3 says; the docs show the script export (TECH-47) on the first page.

ears.if: AutoMigrate is on and the stored schema version is older than the expected version
ears.shall: apply the embedded migrations up to the expected version and log what it did

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: concurrent starts are serialised by a store-side migration lock (REQ-42, TECH-126).

ears.if: AutoMigrate is off and the stored schema version is more than one version older than the expected version
ears.shall: fail the host's start with a message that includes the path of the migration script

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a node accepts the schema version it expects or one version older, so library N+1 runs on schema N as STO-5 and NFR-18 require. A newer schema is REQ-43. Migrations therefore stay additive within a major version (TECH-127). StartupFailed fails the host's start (refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-10, owner's choice of the recommended option).

sources.quote: a version mismatch MUST fail fast at startup with the script path in the message

ears.when: a migration that is already applied is applied again
ears.shall: leave the schema unchanged

sources.quote: Migrations are embedded, versioned and idempotent.

ears.shall: keep retrying the connection with backoff without stopping the host, and claim no job until the store is reachable

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: Bellhop runs inside the application's host, so a database outage must not take the web application down. The health check reports Unhealthy meanwhile (REQ-31). The docs should advise mapping Bellhop health to readiness, not liveness, or the orchestrator restarts the pod in a loop.

ears.if: the node's clock differs from the database clock by more than ClockSkewThreshold
ears.shall: log a warning that names the measured skew

sources.quote: Bellhop MUST warn when node clock skew exceeds a threshold.

ears.shall: stop claiming new jobs on that node
give in-flight jobs ShutdownTimeout to finish after the host stops, 30 seconds by default (ShutdownTimeout)

ears.when: every in-flight job has finished, or ShutdownTimeout has passed, the remaining jobs' tokens were cancelled and the lease releases and cancellations that jobs REQ-140 and REQ-190 call for at shutdown were attempted
ears.shall: stop the node

requirements.notes: The job side (cancel token, release lease, job returns to Enqueued) is REQ-140 in the jobs module. The release is best-effort (refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-5, recommended option): a release that fails because the store is down is covered by lease expiry (jobs REQ-132), and that attempt then counts, so a store outage never blocks shutdown. jobs run 3 F-1: a job whose timeout token was signalled is not released (jobs REQ-140). It stays in flight until jobs REQ-138 or REQ-186 settles it, so the drain waits for it up to ShutdownTimeout like any other job; with the defaults (both 30 s) a timeout signalled before the stop signal settles within the drain. Only a handler that jobs REQ-138 or REQ-186 has not settled when the node stops is left to lease expiry, and its attempt counts (jobs REQ-132, REQ-133). refiner-model 2026-11-07 run 4 F-1 (recommended option): the earlier note said the drain does not wait for it, which the sentence never said. jobs run 4 F-1 (recommended option): the node also waits for the cancellations jobs REQ-190 makes at shutdown, so a job whose cancellation was requested before the node's shutdown check (jobs REQ-140, REQ-190) ends Cancelled at a graceful stop, even at its last attempt; without the wait, lease expiry dead-lettered it (jobs REQ-133). jobs run 7 and run 8 F-1: a request made after that check is not part of the shutdown. Only a timed-out handler still in its grace period can be in flight then; the node does not wait for it, and the job's ordinary rules decide, the handler's own outcome until the node stops and lease expiry (jobs REQ-132, REQ-133) after it, as after a crash.

ears.if: an internal error (store error, scheduler error, serialization error or recovery error) is stalling processing
ears.shall: report the node Unhealthy

requirements.notes: Turned into a health check (refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-3, recommended option) so that REQ-35's 'every check has passed' covers it and the node cannot report Healthy while the stall lasts. Same health-check event as REQ-31 to REQ-35, REQ-44 and REQ-58.

sources.quote: An error that would stall processing MUST also flip the health check.

ears.shall: report the node Unhealthy

ears.if: the stored schema version is neither the expected version nor one version older
ears.shall: report the node Unhealthy

requirements.notes: Follows from the accepted range (REQ-23): once the first N+1 node migrates during a rolling deploy, nodes still on N see a newer schema and report Unhealthy until they are replaced. They keep working meanwhile because migrations are additive (TECH-127).

ears.if: the node's worker loop is not alive
ears.shall: report the node Unhealthy

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: only nodes with a worker have a worker loop; a client- or dashboard-only process is not reported Unhealthy for lacking one.

ears.if: no check that reports Unhealthy fails, and scheduling lag exceeds SchedulingLagThreshold, dead-letter growth exceeds DeadLetterGrowthThreshold or failures in the window exceed FailureThreshold
ears.shall: report the node Degraded

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: backlog and failure checks give Degraded; MinNodesAlive gives Unhealthy (REQ-44). Recovery from Unhealthy now always goes through Degraded by REQ-58, backlog or not (refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-8, recommended option), so this rule no longer needs `from: Unhealthy`.

ears.if: every check has passed on the last HealthyAfterPasses runs in a row
ears.shall: report the node Healthy

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: recovery needs consecutive passes so the status does not flap near a threshold. The source only implies recovery. Only from Degraded: an Unhealthy node first drops to Degraded by REQ-58 (refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-8). Health starts Unhealthy (entity `initial`, refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-11, recommended option), so this rule is the only route to Healthy and readiness waits HealthyAfterPasses check intervals after startup.

ears.shall: be delivered in three milestones: M1 core preview (job model, IJobClient, in-memory and PostgreSQL stores, fire-and-forget, delayed and recurring jobs, retries and dead letters, leases and recovery, OpenTelemetry, health check, Bellhop.Testing, read-only dashboard); M2 1.0 (SQL Server, SQLite and Redis stores, continuations, chains and batches, unique and concurrency keys, the full dashboard, BLT-1 to BLT-12, EF Core enqueue, analyzers, conformance suite, docs, benchmark); M3 1.x (BLT-13 to BLT-19, Tier 2 Redis-compatible servers, Garnet fixture, CLI, Native AOT verification, community stores)

requirements.notes: Items in every module carry an M1/M2/M3 tag where the phasing table places them.

ears.shall: record ownership in the store with an expiry rather than as mutual exclusion held by a live connection, and therefore not build on a distributed-lock library

requirements.rationale: ADR-1: claims, leases, recurring triggers, overlap and concurrency keys are all store-side atomic operations; a lock would add a round-trip, hide ownership from the dashboard and recovery, and reproduce Hangfire's lock-timeout failures. The technology constraint is TECH-51.

ears.shall: build the Redis store on sorted sets, lists, hashes and Lua scripts rather than Redis Streams

requirements.rationale: ADR-2: portability across Garnet, Dragonfly, Kvrocks and Upstash; Streams do not model delay, priority or uniqueness; deleting before ack needs Redis 8.2; a lease sorted set gives the same crash recovery. Constraints are TECH-54 and TECH-55.

ears.shall: cover several popular Hangfire add-ons through existing features rather than separate ones: multi-app shared store (namespaces), skip missed runs (misfire Skip), idempotency (unique keys) and options from configuration; jobs addressed by type-name strings are deliberately unsupported

ears.while: a node has no worker registered
ears.shall: run no background duty on that node: no promotion of scheduled or retry jobs, recurring triggers, lease recovery, retention cleanup, outbox relay, Unroutable or orphan sweep, Redis recurring reconciliation, dashboard node-sample pruning or dashboard rollup computation

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: every background duty is part of the worker. Many workers share them safely through store-side atomic operations and leases; a process without AddWorker does none of them. Two changes from refiner-model 2026-11-06: notification checks moved to the alerts registration (REQ-59, owner's decision on integrations F-6), and dashboard sample pruning and rollups were added to the list (dashboard F-8, recommended option). A node taking a metrics sample of itself is not a background duty in this sense (dashboard REQ-314).

ears.shall: not serve the dashboard on that node

requirements.notes: Retired. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the dashboard does not depend on the node mode; an instance serves it exactly when the application maps it (REQ-51).

ears.when: several nodes start at the same time against a store whose schema is older than expected
ears.shall: let only the node holding the store's migration lock apply migrations, and have the others wait for the lock and then re-read the schema version

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. The lock lives in the store (TECH-126), consistent with ADR-1 and TECH-51.

ears.if: the stored schema version is newer than the expected version
ears.shall: fail the host's start with a message that names both versions and says the library is older than the schema

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a node accepts its expected schema or one version older, never a newer one, whether AutoMigrate is on or off. During a rolling deploy a node on N that restarts after an N+1 node migrated fails here; that is acceptable because it is being replaced. Failing the host's start (refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-10, owner's choice) means that restart takes the whole process down, HTTP endpoints included, until the pod is replaced.

ears.if: fewer than MinNodesAlive nodes with the worker registered have sent a heartbeat within NodeLostAfter
ears.shall: report the node Unhealthy

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Every node reports this at the same moment, so an orchestrator that restarts on Unhealthy restarts the whole cluster together; the docs should say so. 'Alive' is defined as in the dashboard's no-worker banner (refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-9, recommended option); NodeLostAfter is defined in REQ-60. Client-only processes do not evaluate it, so a down worker never takes a web API out of readiness; they get the dashboard banner instead.

ears.shall: treat a node as lost after NodeLostAfter without a heartbeat, 5 minutes by default (NodeLostAfter)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (originally integrations REQ-411). refiner-model 2026-11-06 follow-up to dashboard F-13 and hosting F-9: NodeLostAfter is used by hosting REQ-44, dashboard REQ-341 and integrations REQ-404, and heartbeats belong to hosting, so the constant moved here from integrations REQ-411, which is retired.

ears.shall: default ClockSkewThreshold to 5 seconds (ClockSkewThreshold)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06; the source asks for a threshold but gives no value.

ears.shall: default SchedulingLagThreshold to 60 seconds (SchedulingLagThreshold)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06; the source says the thresholds are configurable but gives no defaults.

ears.shall: default DeadLetterGrowthThreshold to 100 dead-lettered jobs in 15 minutes (DeadLetterGrowthThreshold)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.shall: default FailureThreshold to 50 failed attempts in 5 minutes (FailureThreshold)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.shall: default MinNodesAlive to 1 (MinNodesAlive)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Only worker nodes evaluate REQ-44 and a reporting worker node is itself alive, so the default never fires; applications opt in by raising it.

ears.shall: default HealthyAfterPasses to 3 (HealthyAfterPasses)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.shall: serve the dashboard on a node exactly when the application maps it, whether or not the client or the worker is registered

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the dashboard, the client and the worker never talk to each other directly, only through the store. An instance can serve the dashboard with no worker, run a worker with no dashboard, or both.

ears.shall: let a process configure the store with AddBellhop and then register the client (AddClient), the worker (AddWorker) and the alerts registration in any combination, including none, and map the dashboard independently, where registering the worker also makes the client available because handlers enqueue jobs

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06, replacing the node modes of SET-7 (REQ-11 retired). Like Hangfire's AddHangfire / AddHangfireServer split: a web API registers the client and maps the dashboard; a worker service registers the worker. The pieces interact only through the store. The alerts registration was added by the owner on 2026-11-06 (refiner-model, integrations F-6): alerting runs on a worker node, a client or dashboard node, or a node that only does alerts, so a node-lost alert can fire when no worker is alive. Its API name is a TECH matter.

ears.if: code-defined recurring jobs are declared and the worker is not registered
ears.shall: log a warning that this node will not create, update or keep those recurring jobs alive, once, before the node is marked running

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: recurring definitions belong to worker processes (recurring REQ-203 to REQ-207). Event-driven and once, before running (refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-7); same startup event as REQ-16 and REQ-54.

ears.if: Bellhop is configured but none of the client, the worker and the alerts registration is registered and the dashboard is not mapped
ears.shall: log a warning that Bellhop will do nothing on this node, once, before the node is marked running

requirements.notes: Follows from the owner's decision of 2026-11-06 that the client and the worker are both opt-in; without it, a forgotten AddWorker fails silently (P6). Event-driven and once, before running (refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-7); same startup event as REQ-16 and REQ-53.

ears.shall: stop retrying the store connection and mark the node stopped without starting the worker or any background duty

requirements.notes: Added by refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1 (recommended option): REQ-25 can keep a node Starting for as long as a database outage lasts, and without this rule a host stop in that window was followed by REQ-18 starting a worker that claims jobs. Same host-stop event as REQ-27, which covers a running node.

ears.while: a node holds the store's migration lock
ears.shall: keep that node starting, and have a node that leaves starting for any reason release the lock first

requirements.notes: Added by refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-4 (recommended option): a node that failed startup while holding the lock left the other nodes waiting under REQ-42. With StartupFailed failing the host's start (REQ-9, F-10), process exit releases a store-native lock (TECH-126).

ears.shall: assume that build-time tooling (OpenAPI generation, EF Core design-time services) builds the host without starting it

requirements.notes: Added by refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-6 (recommended option): REQ-14 follows from this and REQ-12, because neither REQ-12 nor REQ-18 checks for build tooling. The conformance tests check the assumption against the listed tools.

ears.if: no check that reports Unhealthy fails
ears.shall: report the node Degraded

requirements.notes: Added by refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-8 (recommended option): recovery always goes Unhealthy → Degraded → Healthy after HealthyAfterPasses passes (REQ-35), so a recovering node with a backlog never reports better than one without. Same health-check event as REQ-30 to REQ-35 and REQ-44.

ears.while: a node does not have the alerts registration
ears.shall: run no notification check on that node, whether or not the worker is registered

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (refiner-model, integrations F-6): alerting is a separate registration that can live on a worker node, a client or dashboard node, or a node that does only alerts, so the node-lost alert still fires when the last worker is down. The checks themselves, and how several alerts nodes share them, are in the integrations module.

scenarios.title: No store in Production falls back to memory, loudly
scenarios.given: A node starts in the Production environment with no store configured and valid options.
scenarios.then: The node is Running on the in-memory store and exactly one warning about it was logged.

scenarios.title: Invalid option stops startup
scenarios.given: A node starts with PollInterval set to a negative value in configuration.
scenarios.then: The node is StartupFailed, the message names PollInterval and the fix, and no job was claimed.

scenarios.title: Schema mismatch stops startup
scenarios.given: A node starts with AutoMigrate off and a store whose schema is two versions behind.

steps.note: node tries to start workers anyway

scenarios.title: Graceful shutdown
scenarios.given: A running node has two in-flight jobs; one finishes within ShutdownTimeout and one ignores cancellation.

steps.note: timeout passes, the remaining job's token is cancelled and its lease released

scenarios.then: The node is Stopped, it claimed nothing after the host stopped, and the second job is available to other nodes.

scenarios.title: Rolling deploy: new node runs on the previous schema
scenarios.given: Library version N+1 starts with AutoMigrate off against a store on schema version N; the store is reachable and options are valid.
scenarios.then: The node is Running on schema N and no migration was applied.

scenarios.title: Store down at startup keeps the host up
scenarios.given: A node starts while the database is unreachable.
scenarios.then: The host is still running, the node is Starting and reports Unhealthy, and no job was claimed.

glossary.client: AddClient(): IJobClient for application code; included in the worker (REQ-52).
glossary.worker: AddWorker(...): job execution plus every background duty except notification checks (REQ-52, REQ-40).
glossary.alerts: The alerts registration: runs the notification checks (integrations module) on a node, independently of the client and the worker; a node may do only alerts (REQ-52, REQ-59).
glossary.MigrationLock: Store-side lock that serialises schema migrations across starting nodes; held only by a starting node (REQ-42, REQ-56, TECH-126).
glossary.ShutdownTimeout: Time in-flight jobs get to finish after the host stops; 30 s by default (REQ-28).
glossary.AutoMigrate: Whether a node applies embedded schema migrations at startup; true by default (REQ-21).
glossary.ClockSkewThreshold: Node-versus-database clock difference above which a warning is logged; 5 s by default (REQ-45).
glossary.SchedulingLagThreshold: Scheduling lag above which the node reports Degraded; 60 s by default (REQ-46).
glossary.DeadLetterGrowthThreshold: Dead-letter growth above which the node reports Degraded; 100 in 15 min by default (REQ-47).
glossary.FailureThreshold: Failed attempts in the window above which the node reports Degraded; 50 in 5 min by default (REQ-48).
glossary.MinNodesAlive: Worker nodes with a heartbeat within NodeLostAfter below which every worker node reports Unhealthy; 1 by default (REQ-49, REQ-44).
glossary.NodeLostAfter: Time without a heartbeat after which a node is considered lost; 5 min by default (REQ-60).
glossary.HealthyAfterPasses: Consecutive passing health runs needed to return to Healthy; 3 by default (REQ-50).
glossary.LeaseDuration: How long a claim stays valid without a heartbeat; defined in the jobs module (REQ-102).
